ops.body:
**Proven pre-existing, and "flaky" is the wrong word.** The full suite was run on a detached worktree at pristine `a222707` — no `branchplan.go`, none of phases A/B/C/D — and `TestDiscoverTimeoutKillsDescendants` fails **identically, at the same 2.52s**, with `read grandchild PID: open .../grandchild.pid: no such file or directory`.

More precise mechanism than first recorded: it does not fail intermittently. It passes 3/3 standalone and the whole `internal/codeexec` package passes alone (17.8s); it fails **deterministically under `go test ./...` parallelism**, because the test polls a hard 2-second wall-clock deadline for a grandchild to write its pid file and under whole-suite load that grandchild isn't scheduled in time.

Ruled out as caused by the open-pr work: `internal/codeexec` is unmodified by every phase; `render` — the one package phase A touched that codeexec imports — is not on the `Discover` path (`discover.go` imports stdlib only).

One aggravating factor worth recording: the open-pr changes did make the suite heavier, `internal/cli` going from ~170s at baseline to ~239s. That increases the parallel load the deadline has to survive, so it makes the failure easier to hit — but the baseline is already red, so it is aggravating, not causal.

Fix options: derive the poll deadline from `CCX_EXEC_MCP_TIMEOUT` rather than pinning 2s, or mark the test serial so it doesn't compete with the rest of the suite.
